decision: An end prefix with an optional owned cross feature member, or a basic prefix; then any number of prefix metadata members — as KerML 8.2.4.3.1 states it.
notes:
THE CLAUSE IS FLAGGED MALFORMED AND THIS PRODUCTION IS NOT AFFECTED. The pack reports an unmatched `)` on line 8 of the Features clause. That line is inside the Feature production — its own parentheses close at -1 — and this production's parentheses balance on their own, so it is derived from the clause as written. The repair of Feature is recorded on the Feature unit.

A NOTATIONAL SLIP in the clause: the head is `FeaturePrefix :` with no metaclass and no `=`. Nothing about what parses turns on it.

THE XTEXT NAMES A DIFFERENT PRODUCTION: it writes `OwnedCrossingFeatureMember` where the clause writes `OwnedCrossFeatureMember`. The clause's name is the one in the specification's inventory and is used here; the pilot's is a pilot name.

PrefixMetadataMember is stated differently in the two languages and is split (ADR-0014); this shared unit reaches whichever variant belongs to the grammar it is read in.

FILED WITH OMG: the notational slip recorded above is KERML11-108, item 4. It concerns how the rule is written, not what it accepts, so it is recorded as a citation and not as a deviation.
